title: Plan backwards
hook: Three tasks (10, 15 and 20 min) in a row, due at minute 60.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that the latest start for a chain of tasks is the deadline minus all their durations added up, worked backwards from the last task

misconception: If each task fits before the deadline on its own, the whole plan fits.
objective: Compute a latest start from duration and deadline.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Three tasks (10, 15 and 20 min) in a row, due at minute 60. Three tasks (10, 15 and 20 min) in a row, due at minute 60. Latest start for the first? claims.text: Work back from the deadline through the whole chain: 60 minus 20, minus 15, minus 10 is minute 15. Starting the first task any later makes the last one late.

claims.text: Stage: three tasks run back to back, outline 10, draft 15 and edit 20 minutes, and edit is due at minute 60. The chain starts with outline at minute 50 (50–60, 60–75, 75–95), so edit is 35 minutes late; “Work back from 60” starts outline at 15, so edit ends at 60, on time. The slider moves the whole chain. Reveal sentence: Starting outline at minute S, edit finishes at minute F; it is due at minute 60, so it is on time or N minutes late.
